title: A Categorical Framework for Wave-Particle Complementarity: Continuous Observable Structures and Fourier-Pontryagin Duality
abstract: We present a formulation wave-particle complementarity and the de Broglie relation $λ=h/p$ within the framework of categorical quantum mechanics on rigged Hilbert spaces. Position and momentum are represented by continuous dagger-Frobenius structures associated with the locally compact abelian group $\mathbb{R}$ and its Pontryagin dual. The Fourier transform is the unitary implementation of Pontryagin duality and relates the two observable structures. We show that a general character pairing $χ_p^{(α)}(x)=\exp(ipx/α)$ yields a one-parameter family of unitarily equivalent Fourier transforms. Pontryagin duality therefore determines the structural form of the complementarity, but not the numerical value of Planck's constant. The identification $α=\hbar$ is a physical input fixed by the Weyl commutation relations. With this input, the spatial period of the character yields $λ=h/p$.
summary: This paper develops a highly abstract mathematical framework using category theory and Pontryagin duality to formalize wave-particle complementarity. It demonstrates that the mathematical structure of this complementarity is determined by duality, but the physical scale, embodied by Planck's constant $\hbar$, must be imposed externally via the canonical commutation relations. It offers a deep, structural view of the de Broglie relation.
main_problem: The paper aims to rigorously formulate wave-particle complementarity and the de Broglie relation within the advanced mathematical framework of categorical quantum mechanics.
main_result: It shows that while Pontryagin duality determines the structural form of complementarity, the physical constant $\hbar$ must be supplied externally via the Weyl commutation relations to yield the correct de Broglie relation $\lambda = h/p$.
method: The authors employ categorical quantum mechanics on rigged Hilbert spaces, using continuous dagger-Frobenius structures to represent position and momentum operators, and utilizing Pontryagin duality to relate these structures via the Fourier transform.
model_or_system: The model is the quantum mechanical description of a particle, analyzed using abstract mathematical structures like rigged Hilbert spaces and categorical formalism, rather than a specific physical Hamiltonian or lattice model.
key_observables: Position ($\hat{X}$), momentum ($\hat{P}$), and the associated wave-particle character pairing $\chi_p(x) = \exp(ipx/\hbar)$.
important_parameters: Planck's constant ($\hbar$), the scaling parameter $\alpha$, and the physical constant $h$.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the validity of the categorical structure on Schwartz spaces and treats the identification $\alpha = \hbar$ as a necessary physical input fixed by the Weyl commutation relations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the Fourier correspondence between the position and momentum representations.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing the mathematical setting using categorical quantum mechanics and Pontryagin duality. It then derives the Fourier transform relating the two observable structures, demonstrating that the structural relationship is dictated by duality, while the physical scale ($\hbar$) is fixed by the canonical commutation relations.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly abstract, foundational mathematical underpinning for a core concept in quantum mechanics (complementarity), which could inspire new ways to model measurement processes or quantum field theory structures.
